title: CCBHCs and prospective payment
one_liner: A certified clinic must serve everyone who comes and is paid its daily rate only for people enrolled in Medicaid; WellStone has been such a clinic since July 2024.
why_here: Section 12 sets out the clinic model and the tension inside it. Domain 2 follows the federal grant that prepared for it, Domain 3 reports the access times, Domain 6 lists the quality measures it will require, and the dependency map runs its first link from payers to services.

self_check.q: An adult who is not enrolled in Medicaid and has no other insurance comes to WellStone for therapy. Under Alabama's rules for certified clinics, what follows?
options: The clinic may turn the person away, because the daily rate is not paid for them.
Medicaid pays the daily rate anyway, because the clinic is certified.
The clinic must serve the person, and the daily rate is not paid for that visit.
The federal implementation grant pays the daily rate in Medicaid's place.

self_check.q: The Department reported that the wait for an initial evaluation at WellStone fell from 18 days in January 2025 to less than one day in December. What does that figure establish?

title: Civil commitment and assisted outpatient treatment

why_here: Domain 1 describes the two probate courts and the outpatient program. Domains 3 and 5 follow committed people to beds and to transport, Section 10 places the probate court at Intercept 2, and Domain 6 lists commitment counts among the things that are not published.

why_here: Section 11 rests on four years of federal counts and housing inventories for the Huntsville continuum. Point 8 of the summary in Part I, the dependency map and the Domain 6 table of unpublished figures draw on the same reports.

body: This report was researched and written with Claude, an AI model, on 4 October 2026, working only from public sources: agency pages and documents, budgets, court records, organizations' own published reports and data, and local press where no primary document could be opened. The method has three steps, and each leaves a record a reader can inspect.

The first step is research. The scope file lists 199 web search queries, run before and during two sweeps of research, and the pages they led to were read through an automated page reader. Each statement of fact was recorded as a finding: a claim together with the passage from the source that supports it. The publisher's own document was used wherever it could be read, and the press only where no primary document was reachable. In all, 1,375 findings were recorded and 759 were used.

The second step is writing. Prose was written only after the findings were recorded, and the bracketed numbers in the text lead to the sources behind them. Values are shown as published, and anything the report computed is labeled as its own. Figures recalled from memory or estimated were excluded. Sentences marked as analysis are the report's own reading of the evidence.

The third step is checking. Every block of the report was read against the source passages attached to it by independent checkers that did not write it. There was a first check of all 283 blocks, a second check of the blocks changed after the first, a third check of the blocks changed after the second, and a final consistency pass against the list of

still sits. The largest group, 79, is headed "Not published, as far as this review found." Each item says what is missing, why it matters, where the review looked and how the item could be closed.

The limits follow from that. About fifty pages of WellStone's website refused the reader, so much of what the report says about WellStone's programs rests on the

County figures were not fetched afresh; they come from the checked county table assembled for the statewide report

The report is a draft for review. It has not been approved by

It was prepared for Little Orange Fish, which its statewide report names as the backbone organization for the

Every bracketed number leads to an entry on the References page, which gives the publisher, the date, a summary of what the source establishes and a note on whether it was read in full or in part. Of the 405 references cited when the checks were run, 336 were read in full and 68 in part; 92 are press reports. Where an organization is the only source for a statement about itself, the reference says so.

Three habits help when reading with the method in mind. A verified sentence matches the passage recorded for it, which is a narrower thing than the source being right. A sentence marked as analysis is the report's reading and can be argued with. And a statement that something was not found is dated 4 October 2026 and limited to what was read, so the Open Items page is the place to see what a browser, a phone call or the next review might still turn up.
The report invites the organizations it describes to correct it, and its figures are dated so that a later edition can show what changed.
